article_title: Long-Term Impacts of KIPP Middle Schools on College Enrollment and Early College Persistence
citation: Thomas Coen, Ira Nichols-Barrer, Philip Gleason. (2019). Long-Term Impacts of KIPP Middle Schools on College Enrollment and Early College Persistence. Cambridge, MA: Mathematica. https://www.mathematica.org/
title: Use admissions lotteries at oversubscribed schools to estimate long-term school impacts with randomized treatment and control groups.
description: When a school is oversubscribed and allocates seats by lottery, the lottery creates a randomized controlled trial: students offered admission form the treatment group and non-offered applicants the control group. The article states this design ensures the groups are "similar on average" on observable characteristics such as prior test scores and unobservable characteristics such as motivation and parental support, supporting credible long-term impact estimates.
requirements: A school must be oversubscribed and use an admissions lottery so that offers are effectively randomly assigned among applicants
constraints: Applies to applicants of oversubscribed schools; estimates concern students who applied through the lottery, not all students
target_learners: K-12 students applying to oversubscribed charter middle schools
target_learning_goals: estimating school effects on long-run outcomes such as college enrollment
examples: The KIPP study used 5th or 6th grade admissions lotteries in 2008 or 2009 at 13 oversubscribed KIPP middle schools to form treatment and control groups
key_sources: Thomas Coen, Ira Nichols-Barrer, Philip Gleason. (2019). Long-Term Impacts of KIPP Middle Schools on College Enrollment and Early College Persistence. Cambridge, MA: Mathematica. https://www.mathematica.org/publications/long-term-impacts-of-kipp-middle-schools-on-college-enrollment-and-early-college-persistence

article_title: An Impact that Lasts: KIPP Middle Schools Boost College Enrollment
citation: Thomas Coen, Ira Nichols-Barrer, Philip Gleason. (2019). An Impact that Lasts: KIPP Middle Schools Boost College Enrollment. Cambridge, MA: Mathematica. https://www.mathematica.org/publications/an-impact-that-lasts-kipp-middle-schools-boost-college-enrollment
title: Use oversubscribed-school admissions lotteries to build randomized controlled trials for estimating long-term effects of attending a school of choice
description: When a school of choice has more applicants than seats, its admissions lottery can serve as the randomizer for a causal evaluation. The KIPP study 'uses a randomized controlled trial design to ensure' that students offered admission and students not offered admission 'are similar on average', on observable characteristics such as prior test scores and unobservable ones such as motivation and parental support, permitting unbiased long-term impact estimates.
requirements: The school must be oversubscribed, so that admission offers are determined by a lottery
Enough applicants must be tracked long enough for the outcome of interest to accrue
target_learners: Students applying to oversubscribed schools of choice, here 5th- and 6th-grade middle school applicants
target_learning_goals: Causal estimation of a school's effect on long-term outcomes such as four-year college enrollment
examples: The study followed 1,177 lottery applicants to 13 oversubscribed KIPP middle schools and compared students who received admission offers with those who did not
key_sources: Thomas Coen, Ira Nichols-Barrer, Philip Gleason. (2019). An Impact that Lasts: KIPP Middle Schools Boost College Enrollment. Cambridge, MA: Mathematica. https://www.mathematica.org/publications/an-impact-that-lasts-kipp-middle-schools-boost-college-enrollment

article_title: A Study of the Effect of Talent Search on Secondary and Postsecondary Outcomes in Florida, Indiana, and Texas
citation: Jill M. Constantine, Neil S. Seftor, Emily Sama Martin, Tim Silva, David Myers. (2006). A Study of the Effect of Talent Search on Secondary and Postsecondary Outcomes in Florida, Indiana, and Texas. Washington, DC: U.S. Department of Education. https://www.mathematica.org
title: Assist low-income students to overcome information barriers to college access
description: The report concludes that providing low-income students with practical college-access information supports their college aspirations. It states that "assisting low-income students to overcome information barriers may be effective in helping them achieve their aspirations to attend college," identifying guidance on financial aid and admission applications and campus orientation as key services.
requirements: Delivery of practical information such as guidance on completing financial aid and admission applications and orientation to college campuses
constraints: The report frames this as a suggestion based on quasi-experimental findings from three states, not a tested causal decomposition of program components
examples: Talent Search projects delivered guidance on how to complete financial aid and admission applications and what a college campus looks and feels like
key_sources: Jill M. Constantine, Neil S. Seftor, Emily Sama Martin, Tim Silva, David Myers. (2006). A Study of the Effect of Talent Search on Secondary and Postsecondary Outcomes in Florida, Indiana, and Texas. Washington, DC: U.S. Department of Education. https://www.mathematica.org/publications/a-study-of-the-effect-of-talent-search-on-secondary-and-postsecondary-outcomes-in-florida-indiana-and-texas

citation: Jeremy M. Grimshaw, Liz Shirran, Ruth Thomas, Graham Mowatt, Cynthia Fraser, Lisa Bero, Roberto Grilli, Emma Harvey, Andy Oxman, Mary Ann O'Brien. (2001). Changing Provider Behavior: An Overview of Systematic Reviews of Interventions. Medical Care 39(8). https://doi.org/10.1097/00005650-200108002-00004
title: Overview-of-reviews framework for professional educational and quality assurance behavior change interventions
description: The article organizes the evidence on changing professional behavior by systematically identifying, appraising, and synthesizing systematic reviews rather than primary studies. It covered "systematic reviews of professional behavior change interventions published between 1966 and 1998" and identified "Forty-one reviews... covering a wide range of interventions and behaviors." This review-of-reviews structure maps which intervention families (passive dissemination, educational outreach, reminders, multifaceted approaches) have what kind of evidence, making the literature accessible to decision makers.
requirements: Requires identifying, appraising, and synthesizing existing systematic reviews of professional educational or quality assurance interventions
constraints: The evidence base available to the overview was incomplete, as the article itself states
target_learners: Healthcare professionals whose behavior is the target of educational or quality assurance interventions
target_learning_goals: Translation of research findings into professional practice; improved quality of care
examples: The overview identified 41 systematic reviews published between 1966 and 1998 covering a wide range of interventions and behaviors.
key_sources: Jeremy M. Grimshaw, Liz Shirran, Ruth Thomas, Graham Mowatt, Cynthia Fraser, Lisa Bero, Roberto Grilli, Emma Harvey, Andy Oxman, Mary Ann O'Brien. (2001). Changing Provider Behavior: An Overview of Systematic Reviews of Interventions. Medical Care 39(8). https://doi.org/10.1097/00005650-200108002-00002

article_title: The Effects of Generative Learning Strategy Prompts and Metacognitive Feedback on Learners' Self-Regulation, Generation Process, and Achievement
citation: Lee, Hyeon Woo. (2008). The effects of generative learning strategy prompts and metacognitive feedback on learners' self-regulation, generation process, and achievement. Dissertation in Instructional Systems, The Pennsylvania State University. https://etda.libraries.psu.edu
title: Rubric-based assessment of learners' overt generative strategy products (highlighting and notes) with generalizability-theory reliability checks
description: A performance-based assessment approach that measures the quality of learners' overt use of generative learning strategies from their actual products rather than from log files. The study "gathered and analyzed overt evidence of generative learning from learners' highlighting and note-taking products instead of log files" and "developed a rubric for assessing the quality of learner's overt use of generative learning strategies and applied generalizability theory in order to verify the reliability of performance-based assessment". Quality is defined as how well learners highlight sentences carrying the main idea and take notes in their own words to create relationships and meaning.
requirements: Learners must produce overt artifacts (underlined sentences and notes) on the instructional material that can be rated against the rubric
target_learners: undergraduate students using generative strategy tools
target_learning_goals: measuring quality of selective attention to main ideas and meaning-making note taking
examples: A rubric (Table 3-9) rated learners' highlighting and note products, with variance components estimated under a two-facet crossed p x r x c generalizability design
key_sources: Lee, Hyeon Woo. (2008). The effects of generative learning strategy prompts and metacognitive feedback on learners' self-regulation, generation process, and achievement. Dissertation in Instructional Systems, The Pennsylvania State University. https://etda.libraries.psu.edu

article_title: Differences in the Difficulty of Accessing Various 3-Dimensional Locations Under Mirror-Image Conditions During Laparoscopic Surgery.
citation: Inagaki Yuriko MD, Kawai Kazushige MD, PhD, Sonoda Hirofumi MD, PhD, Anzai Hiroyuki MD, PhD, Nagai Yuzo MD, PhD, Abe Shinya MD, PhD, Yokoyama Yuichiro MD, PhD, Ozawa Tsuyoshi MD, PhD, Kishikawa Junko MD, PhD, Emoto Shigenobu MD, PhD, Murono Koji MD, PhD, Sasaki Kazuhito MD, PhD, Nozawa Hiroaki MD, PhD, Ishihara Soichiro MD, PhD. (2024). Differences in the Difficulty of Accessing Various 3-Dimensional Locations Under Mirror-Image Conditions During Laparoscopic Surgery. Surgical Laparoscopy, Endoscopy & Percutaneous Techniques. https://doi.org/10.1097/SLE.0000000000001087
title: Overcome mirror-image difficulty through both environmental adjustment (monitor, camera, line-of-sight positioning) and training
description: The article proposes attacking mirror-image difficulty on two fronts: adjusting the operating environment — the positioning of monitor, camera, and the surgeon's line of sight, including camera rotation tactics — and building skill through training. The authors state "the difficulty of mirror-image can be overcome by training", citing their previous finding that difficulties "can be overcome to a significant degree after 4 days of training", and the present finding that difficulty decreased with surgical experience.
requirements: Access to monitor/camera repositioning options or side monitors, and dedicated training time in a box trainer
constraints: Digitally flipping or inverting the monitor image is disorientating because anatomy appears on the opposite screen side, and may not be a final solution when forceps move over a wide area
target_learning_goals: performing laparoscopic maneuvers accurately under mirror-image conditions
examples: The authors' prior study found mirror-image manipulation difficulties were overcome to a significant degree after 4 days of training
